title: World data manifest
description: Every external dataset the Phase 0 world data pipeline consumed, with its source, URL, date retrieved, version, digest, and any gap or substitution. Generated by the run that produced the data, so it cannot drift from what was actually read.

datasets.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program, Vintage 2023 Sub-County Population Estimates (SUB-EST2023)
datasets.licence: U.S. Government work, public domain (Title 17 U.S.C. 105). No permission needed to redistribute.
datasets.used_for: Settlement population. Imports the CENSUS2020POP column, the published decennial count.
datasets.sha256_verification: No upstream digest is published for this file, so no comparison against the publisher is possible. The digest below is the one this pipeline computed; the recorded-digest check on later runs catches any change to the local copy. This is logged as a gap in the Data notes.
datasets.notes: One row per incorporated place and Census-designated place. Contains both the 2020 Census count and the later estimate; the pipeline imports the census column only, so every settlement population is a published decennial figure.

datasets.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program, Vintage 2023 Annual Estimates of the Resident Population by State
datasets.licence: U.S. Government work, public domain (Title 17 U.S.C. 105). No permission needed to redistribute.
datasets.used_for: State profile resident population, and the population rating dimension.
datasets.sha256_verification: No upstream digest is published for this file, so no comparison against the publisher is possible. datasets.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Cartographic Boundary Files, 2023, 500k state
datasets.licence: U.S. Government work, public domain (Title 17 U.S.C. 105). No permission needed to redistribute.
datasets.used_for: State boundaries for the map, and state land/water area via the ALAND and AWATER fields.
datasets.sha256_verification: No upstream digest is published for this file, so no comparison against the publisher is possible. datasets.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Cartographic Boundary Files, 2023, 500k place
datasets.licence: U.S. Government work, public domain (Title 17 U.S.C. 105). No permission needed to redistribute.
datasets.used_for: Settlement boundary polygons, longitude and latitude of the interior point, and placed area.
datasets.sha256_verification: No upstream digest is published for this file, so no comparison against the publisher is possible. datasets.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Regional Economic Accounts, GDP and Personal Income by State, SAGDP1 and SAGDP2 (2023 release)
datasets.licence: U.S. Government work, public domain (Title 17 U.S.C. 105). No permission needed to redistribute.
datasets.used_for: Economic output, plus the mining and agriculture value-added series for the metal, gold and food dimensions.
datasets.sha256_verification: No upstream digest is published for this file, so no comparison against the publisher is possible. The digest below is the one this pipeline computed; the recorded-digest check on later runs catches any change to the local copy. This is logged as a gap in the Data notes.
datasets.notes: The archive holds SAGDP1 (the summary table: GDP, compensation, gross operating surplus) and SAGDP2 (GDP by industry for every BEA line). SAGDP2 is what separates oil and gas extraction from mining except oil and gas, and it separates agriculture from forestry and fishing. The URL is SAGDP.zip rather than SAGDP1.zip: the single-table file 404s, and only the combined archive is published at that path.

declared_gaps.gap: Per-state physical mineral production tonnage by commodity
declared_gaps.why_missing: The authoritative source is the USGS Minerals Yearbook Area Reports, published as PDF tables. www.usgs.gov refused automated requests from this network, and the Mineral Commodity Summaries data releases on USGS ScienceBase carry national and world tables rather than state breakdowns. There is no machine-readable state-by-commodity series.
declared_gaps.substitution: Bureau of Economic Analysis mining-sector value added (SAGDP1), split into fuel and non-fuel lines, combined with USGS MRDS mine-feature counts and commodity mix. Both are real published series covering all 51 jurisdictions. Neither is a tonnage.
declared_gaps.honesty: mining_tonnes is NOT produced. The export carries mining_gva_fuel, mining_gva_nonfuel, mine_feature_count and the commodity mix, and each is labelled with what it actually is.

declared_gaps.why_missing: The Census TIGER/Line ROADS layer for the whole country is a multi-gigabyte download and is not a Phase 0 cost. Primary and secondary roads are downloaded instead.
declared_gaps.substitution: Primary, secondary and other roads from the TIGER/Line PRIMARYROADS layer. Travel time uses the MTFCC road class for speed, so an unclassified local street is treated as a secondary road rather than as fast as a highway.
declared_gaps.honesty: The route graph is a highway-and-secondary network, not a street network. A march that should have used a residential street will not find one.

declared_gaps.gap: Rail line operating status and year opened
declared_gaps.wanted_for: route graph, historical road gating (ERA.md section 5)
declared_gaps.substitution: All rail lines are imported. Rail is not used for travel-time gating because the era decision is still open in CHANGELOG.md.
declared_gaps.honesty: An abandoned rail line routes the same as an active one. This matters only if the era decision selects historical road gating.

declared_gaps.gap: Settlement-level farmland, food production, and sanitation
declared_gaps.wanted_for: settlement seed fields from CAUSE_EFFECT.md section 2
declared_gaps.why_missing: USDA publishes farmland by state, not by place. No federal series gives cropland, food output, or sewerage coverage per settlement.
declared_gaps.substitution: Settlement food production is apportioned from its own state's USDA ERS cropland in proportion to settlement population, which is stated on every output row. Sanitation starts from a documented config constant, not from a measurement.
declared_gaps.honesty: settlement food_production is an apportionment, not a measurement. settlement sanitation is a constant plus a population term, not a measurement. Both carry a source_apportionment flag so no consumer mistakes them for observed data.

declared_gaps.gap: Historical population for an earlier start year
declared_gaps.wanted_for: ERA.md section 5, per-year state profile recomputation
declared_gaps.why_missing: The era decision is still open in CHANGELOG.md, so no start year has been chosen. The pipeline is parameterised on census_year and currently uses 2020.
declared_gaps.substitution: Census {year} decennial counts, which is the nearest real published decade to the late era band. Changing config census_year plus adding the matching Census file is the whole cost of moving to another decade.
declared_gaps.honesty: Ratings are for the 2020 census vintage. They are not valid for a 1950 start year until the pipeline is re-run against that decade's Census files.

boundaries: cb_2023_us_state_500k.zip: read 56 boundaries. Projection as published: GEOGCS["GCS_North_American_1983",DATUM["D_North_American_1983",SPHEROID["GRS_1980",6378137,298.257222101]],PRIMEM["Greenwich",0],UNIT["Degree",0.017453292519943295]]

boundaries: 33 of 56 state boundaries are multipolygons in the source file (main body plus islands and lake shorelines). Rings were grouped by winding order, so islands are separate polygons rather than holes in the mainland.

boundaries: Pipeline-computed polygon area was compared against the Census ALAND field for every state; the largest disagreement was 16.45% (Alaska). That is the expected difference between a computed area and the Census Bureau's own published figure, and is why the pipeline uses the published figure.

boundaries: Area figures are the Census Bureau's own ALAND and AWATER values from the boundary file attribute table, converted from square metres to square kilometres. They are not areas this pipeline computed from the polygons.
boundaries: cb_2023_us_place_500k.zip: read 32608 place boundaries. Longitude and latitude are the area-weighted centroid of the boundary's main body, with islands and lake areas excluded.

boundaries: Most common Census LSAD area-type codes present: 57 (community, 12587), 25 (city, 10200), 43 (other, 4345), 47 (other, 3937), 21 (borough, 1215), 55 (other, 214). The code is carried through to the export rather than being replaced with a guess.

boundaries cross-check: Largest bounding-box difference between the two files was 0.5548 degrees (Wisconsin). Reported, not enforced: the two publishers generalise coastlines very differently and assign shared waters such as the Great Lakes differently.

boundaries cross-check: Note recorded from the real data: Natural Earth's own 'fips' property is wrong for Kentucky (it carries US21, Maryland's code), so the match uses 'iso_3166_2' instead. ports: ne_10m_ports.geojson: 1081 ports in the file, 81 of them attributed to one of the 51 states by testing each port point against the real state polygons. The remaining ports are outside US state boundaries in this source.

ports: Port importance uses Natural Earth's own scale rank. The ranks this file actually uses for ports are 3 to 8 (minor, intermediate, small); it contains no rank 0-2 feature, so no port is labelled major and none is treated as more important than the source claims. Natural Earth publishes no throughput figure in this file, so no tonnage is imported and none is assumed.

ports: Antimeridian: Alaska's boundary spans 359 degrees of longitude because the Aleutians cross the 180th meridian, so a port point is also tested shifted by a full turn. As it happens no port in this file lies west of 170 degrees west, so the shift currently attributes nothing extra. It is kept because it is correct, not because the data needed it.

state profiles: BEA SAGDP: applied 458 state-by-industry values, all in millions of 2023 current dollars. GDP comes from SAGDP1 line 3 and is cross-checked against the SAGDP2 all-industry total in build_state_profiles's assertion step.

state profiles: USDA ERS Major Land Uses: attached land use to 51 states, in 1,000 acres as the workbook title states, converted to hectares with the exact definition of an acre. ERS notes that distributions may not add to totals because of rounding.

state profiles: USGS MRDS: read 304632 mine features worldwide, matched 51 of 51 states by state name. 0 states have no matched mine feature at all, which is reported rather than read as zero production.

state profiles: Commodity grouping is keyword matching over the real USGS commodity strings. 27927 US features carried a commodity string that matched none of the configured groups; those are counted per state in mine_commodities_unmatched rather than being forced into a group.

state profiles: BEA cross-check: SAGDP1 current-dollar GDP and the SAGDP2 all-industry total were compared for 51 states; the largest disagreement was 0.0000% (Alabama), inside the 0.1000% tolerance.

sections: Section membership is transcribed from FACTIONS.md sections 4.1 to 4.6 and matched to FIPS codes against the Census Bureau's own state list. No state code was typed by hand, which matters: an earlier draft of this config used alphabetical positions as if they were FIPS codes and would have put California in the Mountain Alliance.

sections: All 51 jurisdictions present in the state profiles - the 50 states plus the District of Columbia - are assigned to exactly one of the six sides, and no side names a state that has no profile. assign_sections raises rather than reporting a partial map, so reaching the ratings at all is the proof.

sections: Section ratings are computed from these real inputs, all of them national totals the pipeline loaded: ag_gva_usd (national 269,200), cropland_ha (national 152,736,860), gdp_current_usd (national 27,673,078), mine_feature_gold (national 87,128), mine_producer_gold (national 42,378), mine_producer_metal (national 48,736), mining_nonfuel_gva_usd (national 77,051), population (national 334,914,895), port_weight (national 21)

sections: Each dimension produces one number per side: a weighted blend of that side's share of the national total for each input in [ratings.weights], so it reads directly as a fraction of the country. The 5 bands are the even division of the interval from one standard deviation below the mean side to one standard deviation above it (span 1.0 standard deviations), which puts 3 on the average side and makes one rating step half a standard deviation of the six sides. The mean and the standard deviation are computed from the real data; the design targets in FACTIONS.md section 3 are read only to be compared against, never to compute a value. The bands are deliberately NOT cut at percentiles of the 51 individual states: a side is an aggregate of 2 to 14 states, so its share of the national total is several times a single state's share and every side lands in the top band on every dimension. That is recorded per dimension in state_share_reference and explained in docs/SECTION_RATINGS.md.
sections: computed 30 ratings across 6 sides x 5 dimensions; 13 match the FACTIONS.md section 3 design target and 17 differ. Ratings were not adjusted to match; see docs/SECTION_RATINGS.md.
